== spec/merkle/test_hashing.md ==

Scenarios S5 and S6 describe a path-style GROUPED tree that
contradicts the architecture. S5 says the `alpha` module node has
children `alpha/module.json` (leaf), `alpha/arch` (interior),
`alpha/impl` (interior), `alpha/flow` (interior), and that
`alpha/arch` groups `alpha/arch_widget.md` / `alpha/arch_gadget.md`.
S6 asserts an `alpha/arch` interior hash and a module hash taken
over [module.json, arch, impl, flow] group hashes.

The refreshed `arch_tree_builder.md` and `impl_tree_construction.md`
describe a FLAT identity-hash tree: a module node's children are
one `meta/<module-hash>` envelope leaf plus one leaf per spec node
(component, impl_section, data_flow, test_section, requirement),
each keyed directly by its 12-char hex identity `id`. There are no
per-type `arch`/`impl`/`flow` interior group nodes and no
path-style keys — `arch_tree_builder.md` lines 66-68 state the
path-style scheme was deleted.

- Rewrite S5 so the `alpha` module node's children are the
  `meta/<module-hash>` leaf and one identity-hash-keyed leaf per
  spec node — no `alpha/arch`/`alpha/impl`/`alpha/flow` interior
  nodes.
- Rewrite S6 so the module interior hash is `HashChildren` over
  [meta leaf hash + each spec-node leaf hash] directly, with no
  intermediate group hashes.
- Update the `## Setup` block so the fixture's components,
  impl_sections and data_flows each carry a 12-char hex identity
  `id`, since leaf keys are read from those `id` fields.

S7, S8, E3, E4 and E5 are structure-agnostic and already
consistent with the flat tree — no change needed.

title: merkle: TreeBuilder and CompletenessChecker re-derive identity hashes instead of reading the id field
description:
TreeBuilder keys two node classes by a re-derived identity hash
rather than reading the node's `id` field directly, contradicting
the merkle spec.

== Spec contract ==

arch_tree_builder.md line 15: "The key of a component,
requirement, impl_section, data_flow, or test_section is exactly
the value of its `id` field." Line 59: project-level requirement
leaves are "keyed by [their] identity hash (`id` field)".
impl_tree_construction.md lines 5 and 9-10: "Every node's key is
the value of its `id` field" / "Key: requirement's `id`".
Requirement 3ada6b800cc5 (Identity-hash tree keying) states
merkle keys must be "identical to mapping-store spec_node_id
values".

== Actual code ==

merkle/tree_builder.go:60 — project-level requirement leaves:
    key := schema.IdentityHash("project", "requirement", req.ID)
This re-hashes an already-hashed id. Project requirement
`d5a8407d38e1` becomes merkle key `3ccc8fb574c3` — NOT equal to
the id field.

merkle/tree_builder.go:104 — module interior nodes:
    moduleHash := schema.IdentityHash("module", mod.Name)
The /spec skill happens to generate module ids the same way, so
the output equals mod.ID — output-equivalent but still not read
from the `id` field as the spec requires.

== Why all tests pass ==

merkle/completeness_checker.go uses the SAME derivation:
- lines 62 / 298: IdentityHash("module", m.Name)
- line 70: projReqByTreeKey keyed by
  IdentityHash("project","requirement", req.ID)
- line 304: IdentityHash("project","requirement", req.PreqID)
So the merkle module is internally consistent and the suite is
green. This is latent drift, not a live failure.

== Origin ==

Leftover from the integer-id era: before the identity-hash-ids
proposal, ids were integers, so a hash had to be derived to get a
12-char hex key. After identity-hash-ids made ids real identity
hashes, the re-derivation became redundant but was never removed.

== Fix ==

A single coordinated change across both components:
- tree_builder.go: key project requirement leaves by req.ID
  directly; key module interior nodes by mod.ID directly.
- completeness_checker.go: drop the matching re-derivations so it
  looks up by req.ID / mod.ID directly.
- merkle/tree_builder_test.go: the current fixtures use
  placeholder ids like "000000000001" for both modules and
  project requirements, which would COLLIDE at the root once both
  are keyed by `id` directly. Give every fixture node a distinct
  realistic identity hash.

Surfaced during /implement of spexmachina-phb.5 (merkle:
TreeBuilder) — see PR#173.

title: merkle: Change.Path field should be Change.Key to match spec and Node.Key
description:
merkle.Change names its identity-hash-key field `Path`, but the
spec interface and the sibling tree type both call it `Key`. The
field holds a spec node's 12-char identity hash (or a `meta/*`
key), never a filesystem path — `Path` is a misnomer left over
from the path-keyed era, before identity-hash tree keying.

== Spec contract ==

spec/merkle/arch_diff_engine.md — the `## Interface` Go block
declares the field as `Key`:

    type Change struct {
        Key      string // identity hash of the spec node ...
        Type     string // "added", "removed", "modified"
        ...
    }

spec/merkle/flow_diff_classification.md — the "DiffEngine ->
ImpactClassifier" data shape also lists it as `key`.

== Actual code ==

merkle/diff_engine.go:29 — the struct field is `Path`:

    type Change struct {
        Path     string     // identity hash key
        Type     ChangeType // ...
        ...
    }

The field's own comment calls it "identity hash key". The sibling
type merkle.Node uses `.Key` everywhere (tree_builder.go,

title: impact: BeadStatus never populated on mapping records, cleanup creates never fire
description:
impact req 3dcf3c279ac5 (Classify cleanup actions for removed nodes) says: a removed spec node with a closed bead must produce obsolete + cleanup create; open/in_progress produces obsolete only. ActionClassifier implements the rule at impact/action_classifier.go:118-128 by checking o.Record.BeadStatus == "closed". mapping.Record has the BeadStatus field (mapping/mapping_store.go:30).

Gap: BeadStatus is never populated on mapping records in production. impact.ReadBeads (impact/bead_reader.go) reads each bead's live status from br list --json into BeadSpec.Status, but cmd/spex/impact.go never calls ReadBeads and never merges BeadSpec.Status into Record.BeadStatus before handing records to MatchNodes. The field stays empty through the whole pipeline, so the closed-bead check at action_classifier.go:119 always evaluates false. No cleanup create has ever been emitted.

Dormant because no prior PR has removed a component whose bead was already closed. PR #128 (data flow contract layer) removes ProposalTagger — a closed bead — so this is the first case to exercise the path.

Fix: in cmd/spex/impact.go runImpactE, after store.List(), call impact.ReadBeads(ctx, beadBin) to get live statuses, build a map keyed by RecordID, and copy Status into each record's BeadStatus field before passing to MatchNodes. Add a --bead-cli flag (default "br") to the impact command so users can select the bead binary (mirrors apply). Tests cover closed, open, in_progress, and missing-bead cases.

title: impact: ActionClassifier leaves Action.Node as identity hash for added data_flows and test_sections
description:
spec/impact/arch_action_classifier.md defines Action.Node as the "affected spec node name" (line 63) and the reason-string templates (lines 80-84) use {node_name}, e.g.:

- "New spec node: {module}/{node_name}"
- "Code cleanup: {module}/{node_name}"

For MODIFIED nodes (matched branch), the code correctly resolves via nodeName(r) which reads r.Component from the mapping record. This works for components.

For ADDED nodes (unmatched branch), impact/action_classifier.go sets:

    node := u.Change.Path

where u.Change.Path is the identity hash, NOT the name. There is no lookup against the current spec graph to resolve the name.

Symptoms observed during apply for proposal 2026-04-18-decouple-spex-from-br:

- Component beads get proper titles: "emit: ChangesetBuilder", "ingest: Reconciler", "adapters: BrReferenceAdapter" (matched or component-only code path).
- Data_flow beads get hashes: "emit: dbe8d1e707d5", "ingest: 6fd1f0cbb76c", "adapters: 703128d3ebd6".
- Multi-component test_section beads get hashes: "emit: 280a5495eef8", "ingest: 2cd902e10873", "ingest: 2515c91337a5".

Reason strings are similarly affected: "New spec node: emit/dbe8d1e707d5" instead of "New spec node: emit/Emit flow".

Fix: in the unmatched branch of ClassifyActions (impact/action_classifier.go ~line 99, and similarly for orphaned/removed at ~line 137 if it uses u.Change.Path), use the `graph mapping.SpecGraph` parameter (already passed in) to resolve the spec node's name from the current module.json by (module, node_type, spec_node_id). Fall back to the identity hash only if the lookup fails (e.g., node truly not in current spec).

Suggested helper signature: `graph.NodeName(module, nodeType, specNodeID) string`.

Tests:
- A unit test that exercises ClassifyActions on an added data_flow and asserts Action.Node equals the data_flow's "name" field from module.json.
- Same for test_section.
- Same for component (regression: should still work).
